record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For the positive-solution system x_{n+1} = b1 x_n/(A1 + y_n), y_{n+1} = (b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(x_n + y_n), with x_0,y_0 > 0, positive parameters, b2 != g2, and A1 + g2 < b1 < A1 + b2, prove or disprove that the unique positive equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable for all positive initial conditions.

with positive initial conditions, is globally asymptotically stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional system of rational difference equations
  x_{n+1} = β₁ x_n / (A₁ + y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (β₂ x_n + γ₂ y_n) / (x_n + y_n),
for n = 0, 1, 2, …, where the parameters β₁, β₂, γ₂, A₁ are positive real numbers with β₂ ≠ γ₂, the initial conditions satisfy x₀ > 0 and y₀ > 0, and the parameters obey
  A₁ + γ₂ < β₁ < A₁ + β₂.

Under these hypotheses the system has a unique positive equilibrium (x̄, ȳ) ∈ (0, ∞)². Prove or disprove that this positive equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable; that is, it is locally asymptotically stable, and for every choice of positive initial conditions (x₀, y₀) the solution (x_n, y_n) converges to (x̄, ȳ) as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2014 paper by L.-X. Hu and X.-M. Jia in Abstract and Applied Analysis ("Global Asymptotic Stability of a Rational System") studies precisely this system and proves that, in the case γ₂ < β₂ (which is equivalent to the hypothesis A₁ + γ₂ < β₁ < A₁ + β₂ since this forces γ₂ < β₁ − A₁ < β₂), the unique positive equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable. This resolves the conjecture in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Global Asymptotic Stability of a Rational System (Hu & Jia, 2014)
status_evidence.snippet: The major conclusion shows that, in the case where γ2 < β2, if the unique positive equilibrium exists, then it is globally asymptotically stable.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that the unique positive equilibrium of the system is globally asymptotically stable under the stated parameter conditions is proved.
